simple.meaning: מַבָּט (mabbâṭ) is a Hebrew word meaning “something expected , i.e. (abstractly) expectation.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַבָּט (H4007) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 20:5, with occurrences in Isaiah, Zechariah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַבָּט (H4007) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַבָּט (H4007) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַבָּט (mabbâṭ) / H4007 is traced through Isaiah 20:5, Isaiah 20:6, Zechariah 9:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4007. mabbat or mebbat [ מַבָּט ] noun masculine Zech 9:5 expectation = object of hope or confidence (literally thing looked to ); — suffix מַבָּטֵנוּ Isa 20:6 , מַבָּטָם 20:5 , מֶבָּטָהּ Zech 9:5 ; — of Cush as ally of Judah Isa 20:5-6 , of Tyre as ally of l'hilistia Zech 9:5 .
